title: Fuel Burn vs Book Figures
dataSources: Pilot logbook (`flightlog:entry`), avionics telemetry (`avionics:telemetry`), flight-sim sessions (`flightsim:session`), pre-flight checklists (`preflight:check`).
app: Pilot and flight-sim telemetry — electronic logbooks (ForeFlight, LogTen Pro), Stratux / GDL90 avionics receivers, and Microsoft Flight Simulator / X-Plane SimConnect sessions — streamed to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=flightlog:entry
| eval gph=round(fuel_gal/hours,1)
| stats avg(gph) as actual_gph by aircraft_type
| eval book_gph=8.5, delta=round(actual_gph-book_gph,1)
| sort - delta
description: Compares your actual fuel burn against the aircraft's published figures, a check on both technique and engine health.
value: A creeping fuel burn can indicate a leaning technique to fix or an engine issue worth a mechanic's look.
implementation: Ingest fuel and hours into `index=personal`; compare actual burn to book figures per type.
visualization: Bar chart of actual versus book fuel burn by type.
grandmaExplanation: It compares how much fuel you actually use against the plane's official figures, a check on technique and engine.
